chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar and Hafsh ibn al-Bakhtari from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him): that he said,

Regarding a man who frees a slave, he said: 'Allah frees one limb of his from the Fire for every limb of the slave.' And he said: 'It is recommended for a man to draw near [to Allah] on the evening of 'Arafah and on the day of 'Arafah by freeing [a slave] and giving charity.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for freeing a slave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, the physical act of freeing a slave is metaphorically linked to the owner's bodily liberation from Hellfire, emphasizing the tangible spiritual merit of manumission. The hadith further contextualizes this practice within the broader Shia devotional calendar, specifically recommending it during the evening and day of 'Arafah to maximize reward through proximity to the Hajj rituals.
